headline: Record fee earnings as assets under management grow
summary_short: KKR's Q3 2026 Fee Related Earnings were a record $1.32 billion, up from $1.03 billion a year ago, while GAAP revenue fell 17.4% y/y to $4.56 billion on lower insurance revenue.
summary_long: Management fees rose to $1.20 billion from $1.06 billion and fee related performance revenues to $326 million from $73 million. AUM reached $804 billion (up 11%) and Fee Paying AUM $648 billion, with $25 billion of organic new capital raised in the quarter. Insurance operating earnings eased to $230 million from $305 million. KKR repurchased $567 million of stock from June 30 to November 4, raised its buyback authorization by $500 million, and declared a $0.195 dividend.
confidence_notes: GAAP revenue and net income come from the shard; segment figures (FRE, AUM) are as stated in the release. GAAP revenue decline is driven by the insurance segment ($2.80B vs $3.78B) and is not a measure of fee-earnings momentum.

drivers.explanation: Insurance revenue fell to $2.8 billion from $3.8 billion while asset management and strategic holdings revenue was roughly flat at $1.76 billion.
Fee Related Earnings increased 24% year over year, driven primarily by growth in management fees and fee related performance revenues.
Growth in Fee Paying AUM from organic new capital raised underpins management fee growth; KKR expects to return over $40 billion to clients in 2026.
